lines.say: This is how git rebase replays your commits.
It copies them, one at a time, onto a new base.
Main has commits A and B.
Your feature branch starts at B and adds D and E.
Then someone adds commit C to main.
Run git rebase main, and git sets D and E aside.
It replays D on top of C, as a new commit.
Then it replays E on top of the new D.
Your branch now points at the last copy.
First, switch to your branch and rebase it onto main.
If a conflict stops the replay, fix it, then continue.
